record.original_question: Given a signed graph Γ = (G, σ), define a complement signed graph Γ̄ = (Ḡ, σ̄) whose underlying graph is the usual graph complement and for which useful spectral relations with the complete signed graph Γ ∪ Γ̄ hold.

evidence.quote: The complement of signed graph should be a signed graph whose underlying graph is the usual complement, however the signature has not been defined in a satisfactory way yet.
Problem 3.29. Given a graph Γ = (G, σ), define the complement Γ = ( G, σ¯) such that there are nice (spectral) properties derived from the complete signed graph Γ ∪ Γ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Γ = (G, σ), where G = (V, E) is a simple finite undirected graph and σ : E → {+1, −1} is a signature on its edges. The adjacency matrix A(Γ) is the symmetric matrix with entries A(Γ)_{uv} = σ(uv) if uv ∈ E and 0 otherwise; the spectrum of Γ is the multiset of eigenvalues of A(Γ). Two signed graphs on the same vertex set are switching equivalent if one is obtained from the other by, for some U ⊆ V, negating the signs of all edges with exactly one endpoint in U; switching equivalent signed graphs are cospectral.

For a signed graph Γ = (G, σ) on vertex set V, let Ḡ = (V, Ē) denote the usual graph-theoretic complement of G (so Ē consists of all unordered pairs of distinct vertices of V that are non-adjacent in G). The signed union Γ ∪ Γ̄ is the signed graph on V whose underlying graph is the complete graph K_{|V|} and whose signature restricts to σ on E(G) and to σ̄ on Ē.

Problem. Define a signature σ̄ : Ē → {+1, −1} on the complement Ḡ, depending only on (G, σ), so that the resulting "complement signed graph" Γ̄ = (Ḡ, σ̄) and the associated signed complete graph Γ ∪ Γ̄ exhibit good spectral behavior — for instance, so that Γ ∪ Γ̄ is well-defined up to switching equivalence and the spectra of Γ and Γ̄ are related to the spectrum of Γ ∪ Γ̄ in a manner analogous to the Laplacian-spectrum relation A(G) + A(Ḡ) = J − I that holds for unsigned graphs.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work titled "On the complement of a signed graph" (Discrete Mathematics, 2025) introduces, via a pseudo-potential construction, a signature on the complement of a signed graph such that the resulting signed complete graph Γ ∪ Γ̄ is stable under switching equivalence, with associated spectral relations. The authors describe this as solving the previously stated open problem on defining the complement of a signed graph.

status_evidence.title: On the complement of a signed graph - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Using a pseudo-potential, one is able to define a signature on the complement of Γ such that the signed complete graph obtained as the union is stable under switching equivalence, providing a solution to an open problem in the literature of signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of defining the complement of a signed graph with good spectral/switching properties has been solved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3.29 asks for a definition of complement Γ̄ = (Ḡ, σ̄) such that there are nice (spectral) properties derived from the complete signed graph Γ ∪ Γ̄.
status_evidence.claim: This is the original formulation of the problem.
